descriptionChirho: The proper-mythological noun Liwyathan meaning 'Leviathan' — the great sea creature of chaos mythology, a named primordial beast that God subdues or will slay; Arabic لِوَيَاثَان (Liwyathan); Korean 리와야탄/레비아탄 (Riwayatan/Rebiatan); Spanish Leviatán; Hindi लिव्यातान (Livyaataan); Swahili Lewiathani. Used in Job 3:8 (those who curse the day, who are ready to rouse Leviathan), Job 41:1 [Heb 40:25] (can you draw out Leviathan with a fishhook?), and Ps 104:26 (Leviathan whom you formed to play in the sea). These passages treat Leviathan as a specific named creature — terrifying, enormous, and under God's sovereign power.

The epithet-mythological use of Liwyathan as 'the twisting serpent, the fleeing dragon' — Leviathan described by its serpentine attributes as a cosmic adversary to be destroyed; Arabic لَوِيَاثَان (Lawiayathan); Korean 레비아단/레비야탄 (Rebiadan/Rebiyatan); Spanish Leviatán; Hindi लिव्यातान (Livyaataan); Swahili Lewiathani. Used in Isa 27:1 (twice: the fleeing serpent, the twisting serpent) and Ps 74:14 (you crushed the heads of Leviathan). English translates as 'serpent' and 'twisting' rather than simply 'Leviathan,' reflecting the descriptive-epithet quality. These passages emphasize Leviathan's serpentine, multi-headed, dragon-like nature in eschatological or creation-conflict contexts, distinct from the passages that treat it simply as a named creature.
